answer: A sealed exam gate blocks bulk identity creation. Each applicant draws one task from a sealed vault of questions and an orchard of jobs, at a time chosen by a beacon, so answers cannot be shared in advance. The k-th fake identity needs its seat, proctor, and pass: 1,000 fakes need 1,000 seats at 40 credits each, 40,000 credits total, rising linearly with no reuse of a passed exam. The named failure mode is answer rental: a rented answer fails because the beacon reseeds the task and the vault releases a different question. An honest agent pays once and keeps full rights.
